page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-6xCPU-16GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 6 shared vCPUs mapped to 6 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7542 processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of x86_64 system memory, providing approximately 2.67 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between raw CPU compute and memory throughput. The shared CPU allocation results in poor single-core stress-ng performance of 787.9 and weak multi-core stress-ng performance of 4703.94. However, memory bandwidth is relatively stable, with cached read-only small block operations reaching 616.67 GB/sec and uncached large block reads at 43.56 GB/sec, both falling in the average tier. Large block write bandwidth is weaker at 24.88 GB/sec. Passmark CPU and memory scores align with average tiers, and Redis SET operations perform at an average rate of 8.81 million operations per second.

Given the shared CPU architecture and weak multi-core performance, this server is not recommended for intensive compute tasks or large-scale LLM inference, as evidenced by weak 7B model inference speeds. However, average performance in database operations, bzip3 decompression, and Redis operations makes it a cost-efficient option for budget-conscious workloads. It is appropriate for lightweight web serving, development environments, and small-scale database or caching tasks where continuous, dedicated CPU performance is not a strict requirement.
